query: Equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni and its quaternary and ternary subsets provide 16 candidate alloys, nine of which are single-phase FCC after thermomechanical processing. Early reports associated increasing constituent count with greater strength, but that simple relationship is no longer generally accepted. Despite extensive experimental and theoretical investigation, the origins of differences in deformation and failure behavior remain unresolved; practical interpretation must also account for constituent cost and overall cost-performance balance. What testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs these mechanical-property differences and why? Define a controlled investigation, the observations predicted relative to the equiatomic quinary baseline, the limits within which the hypothesis should apply, the prior evidence supporting it, and an observation that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: The differences in mechanical properties among equiatomic Cr–Mn–Fe–Co–Ni alloys and their quaternary and ternary subsets are governed by how variations in local lattice distortions and stacking fault energies (SFEs) influence dislocation core structures and mobility. Reduced chemical complexity in the subsets lowers local lattice distortion, thereby decreasing the activation barrier for dislocation motion relative to the equiatomic quinary baseline.
generation.material_initial_state: Single-phase FCC alloys produced via identical thermomechanical processing, including the equiatomic Cr–Mn–Fe–Co–Ni and its quaternary and ternary subsets.
generation.intervention: Conduct controlled compression testing using strain-rate jumps alongside dislocation characterization (via TEM) and DFT atomic displacement analyses to assess SFEs for each alloy.
generation.conditions: Experiments performed on single crystals or well-annealed polycrystalline samples with comparable grain size and orientation at room temperature, under controlled strain rates to isolate thermal activation behavior.
generation.structural_mediator: Local lattice distortions and stacking fault energies
generation.mechanism: Variations in alloy composition modulate the degree of local chemical disorder, which alters lattice distortions. These distortions affect the core structure of dislocations by changing the SFE landscape, thereby altering the thermal activation energy required for slip. In alloys with fewer constituents, the reduced distortion leads to lower dislocation activation barriers and a corresponding decrease in yield strength.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the equiatomic quinary alloy, quaternary and ternary alloys will exhibit lower yield strengths in compression tests, reduced activation energies derived from strain-rate jump analysis, and evidence of increased dislocation mobility as seen in TEM. DFT calculations should predict lower SFEs for these simplified alloys.
generation.baseline: Mechanical response of the equiatomic Cr–Mn–Fe–Co–Ni single-phase FCC alloy under identical test conditions.
generation.boundary: This hypothesis applies to single-phase FCC alloys with similar microstructures processed under controlled thermomechanical conditions and within typical room-temperature and moderate strain-rate regimes. Deviations due to secondary phases or extrinsic environmental effects are outside these limits.
generation.uncertainty: Exact quantitative differences in activation barriers and yield strength among the compositions remain uncertain due to sensitivity to processing conditions and potential minor microstructural variations.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare single-phase FCC samples of equiatomic Cr–Mn–Fe–Co–Ni, its quaternary, and ternary subsets. Perform compression tests incorporating strain-rate jumps to extract activation energies and activation volumes. Complement these tests with TEM to analyze dislocation structures and perform DFT calculations to estimate SFEs for each composition.
measurements: Activation energy for dislocation motion from strain-rate jump analysis
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the quaternary and ternary alloys do not show significantly lower yield strengths and activation energies, and if dislocation structures and DFT-calculated SFEs do not differ in a manner consistent with the hypothesis relative to the quinary baseline, then the hypothesis that local lattice distortions and associated SFE changes control the mechanical-property differences is falsified.
